_what_this_is: How big the island is inside Unreal, in centimetres, as measured by Content/Python/measure_ue_island.py. The gate's env.ue_island_measured row reads bbox_cm and compares it against the Blender source in Docs/qa/graybox_spec_report.json.
_why_it_exists: On 2026-10-04 the 180 x 100 plate was applied and verified in the .blend, and env.island_sized went PASS. The FBX Unreal consumes still measured 19.3 x 10.7 and the .uasset had been imported from it five days earlier. Every gate row read the Blender source of truth; none read the artefact the game is built from. A player would have stood on a 19 m island while the report said 180 m.
_status: SEEDED EMPTY. Nobody has run the in-editor measurement yet. bbox_cm is null on purpose and the gate reads MISSING, not FAIL - nobody has measured it, which is not the same as it being wrong.
_how_to_fill: 1. Open the level in Unreal and run Content/Python/measure_ue_island.py (Scripting workspace, or execute_python_script via MCP).
2. It writes bbox_cm and the rest of this file. It only reads - it spawns nothing and saves no level.
3. Commit what it writes. That file is the only evidence the engine has the plate.
If bbox_cm comes back near 1930 x 1070 rather than 18000 x 10000, the asset was
never re-imported. The order that fixes it:
c. re-import the FBX over the existing SM_IslandTop asset
d. re-place the island actor if its transform changed
e. re-run measure_ue_island.py and commit the result
Step (e) is the one that gets skipped, and skipping it is how the plate went
missing for a day with nothing going red.
_units: bbox_cm is Unreal centimetres. The gate divides by 100 to compare against Blender metres, and states the tolerance in metres so a mistaken conversion is visible rather than silent.
